children: Urals crude prices at Russia's Baltic and Black Sea ports rose to their highest levels in three months in early September, according to Reuters monitoring and LSEG data.

Free-on-board prices for Urals crude for loading at Primorsk, Ust-Luga and Novorossiysk this week rose above $80 per barrel for the first time since June 4, as global oil nears $100 after new Middle East strikes fueled supply risks.
The average monthly Urals FOB prices stood above $80 per barrel in April and May amid tensions between the United States and Iran, but slipped below $70 per barrel during the summer months.

Reuters estimates the current spot rouble-denominated tax price of Urals at around 7,000 roubles ($82.12) per barrel, well above the 5,440 roubles per barrel assumption of a basket comprising Urals crude and the higher-priced ESPO Blend grade used in calculating Russia's 2026 federal budget revenues.
Changes in the Urals tax price have a significant impact on Russia's oil and gas tax revenues and overall budget income.
